answer: Bind each epoch's proof to durable unique storage, not momentary compute. Each identity must hold a large random file assigned to it and answer random spot-checks every epoch proving the bytes are still retrievable. One honest agent forges a single store once and keeps it through the long voyage of many epochs. A farm cannot reuse one file across a thousand heads: each head's challenges address its own distinct data, so it must durably hold a thousand separate stores or fail the checks. The fable that compute is cheap in bulk breaks against standing per-identity storage.
